name: Canadian single-mine gold producer (underground mine and mill in northern Ontario, Toronto head office)
modelled_on: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (Eagle River underground mine, Mishi open pit and Eagle River mill near Wawa, Ontario; Toronto head office; Kiena property in Val-d'Or, Quebec), with site practice from the Island Gold (Alamos Gold) and Macassa (Kirkland Lake Gold) technical reports and open pit practice from the Hardrock (Greenstone Gold Mines) feasibility study. Mine, mill, fleet and underground labour corrected on 2026-11-24 from the Eagle River technical reports (SRK 2022, Wesdome 2016)
summary: The company mines gold ore underground at one mine in northern Ontario, about 1.5 hours by road from the nearest town, and turns it into doré bars at its own mill 16.6 km by road from the mine portal. Ore is hoisted up a shaft to a dump near the top of the mine, trucked out the ramp to a surface pad and hauled to the mill by surface trucks. A small satellite open pit, mined by a contractor, added ore until 2020. The mine produces about 90,000 to 120,000 ounces of gold a year from roughly 600 to 800 tonnes of high-grade ore a day. The mill recovers gold by gravity concentration and cyanide leaching with zinc precipitation (the Merrill-Crowe process), filters its tailings and stacks them dry. The doré is trucked by a secure carrier to the Royal Canadian Mint and the refined gold is sold at spot to financial institutions, the company's only revenue, about C$165-290 million a year. About 250 company employees work at the site, underground crews on long rotations and mill crews on 12-hour shifts seven days on and seven off, living in camps while on shift; a mining contractor supplies about 36 more people underground. Production samples go by daily shuttle to the company's assay office in town. A head office of about 18 people in Toronto handles finance, gold sales, disclosure, legal and investor relations for the listed company. The site is organised into mine operations, technical services (engineering and geology), processing with the assay office, maintenance, health, safety and environment, and site administration under a general manager who reports to the chief operating officer. An exploration team drills near the mine and on a property in Quebec that is on care and maintenance. The mine is regulated by Ontario labour, mining and environment ministries, federal effluent rules and securities regulators.

demand_drivers.name: Underground ore tonnes mined and hoisted

evidence.note: Eagle River milled 122,405 t in 2019 (10,200 t/month) and 196,441 t in 2020 (16,370 t/month); 2021 target over 600 tpd (about 18,000 t/month).
168,809 t milled in 2019 and 236,297 t in 2020 including the open pit.
Typical for a narrow-vein underground gold mine at 500-700 tpd; one development crew advances 4-6 rounds a shift-day across several headings.
Fleet list in the resources section; comparable Ontario mines run larger fleets for larger tonnages.
Estimated for a remote mine spending about C$80-120M a year on operating and capital purchases.

demand_drivers.name: People on the site roster (employees and contractors)

evidence.note: About 280 site employees plus 50-150 contractors depending on drilling and shutdown activity.
Derived from 2021 guidance of 164,000-174,000 m at the mine (surface and underground) plus Quebec drilling; 2019-2020 programmes were somewhat smaller.
Face, muck, mill process and some definition core samples at about 250-350 samples a day.

process_map.name: Shift line-up and short-interval control
process_map.description: At the start of each 12-hour shift the supervisor reads the previous shift's report, checks which equipment is available, assigns crews to headings and stopes, and calls progress by radio during the shift. Missing equipment, a blocked ramp or an unsafe heading forces reassignments that ripple through the plan.

evidence.note: Two shifts a day every day on 14/14 rotation, as in job postings for the reference mine (not opened); line-up practice is common underground practice.

process_map.name: Lateral development drilling and blasting
process_map.description: A development crew scales and inspects the face, drills a 3.5-4 m round with a two-boom jumbo, charges it with explosives from the magazine and blasts at shift change. Advance depends on the jumbo being free, services reaching the face and the previous round being supported in time.

evidence.note: 450-700 m a month at about 3.8 m a round; jumbo drill-and-blast is the standard method at Ontario narrow-vein gold mines.

process_map.name: Ground support installation
process_map.description: After the round is mucked, a bolter operator scales loose rock and installs rock bolts and mesh to the pattern in the ground control standard, adding shotcrete or cable bolts in poor ground. No one may work under unsupported ground, so a late bolter holds the whole heading.

evidence.note: Comparable Ontario mine requires support before entry on a one hole, one bolt basis at a 1.2 m pattern; volume is rounds plus rehabilitation.

process_map.name: Longhole stope drilling
process_map.description: Production miners set up a longhole drill on the released stope layout, drill the rings and the slot raise, and record hole depths and deviations for survey. Bad holes or squeezed ground mean redrills that delay the blast and can dilute the stope.

evidence.note: Longitudinal and transverse longhole stoping at comparable mines; 5-8 stopes a month at 2,000-3,500 t each is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Stope charging and blasting
process_map.description: Production miners clean and measure the drilled holes, charge the slot and rings with explosives in a sequence designed by engineering, and blast at shift change after the area is cleared. Misfires, hung-up rings and overbreak are the main problems and some need re-drilling.

evidence.note: Stopes are usually blasted in several firings (slot, then ring groups), about 4-6 per stope.

process_map.name: Mucking and haulage
process_map.description: LHD operators muck development rounds and stopes, using remote control in open stopes, and load trucks that haul ore to the shaft loading pocket and waste to backfill or surface. Truck queues, ramp traffic and loader breakdowns set the daily tonnage.
process_map.unit_of_work: one shift of mucking and haulage

evidence.note: Two shifts a day; loading and hauling 550-650 t of ore plus waste per day.

process_map.name: Shaft hoisting
process_map.description: Hoist operators skip ore from the loading pocket below the 460 m level to a dump at the 70 m level, where underground trucks load at a chute and haul it out the ramp to the surface ore pad. A loading pocket operator runs the pocket by hand, and the cage carries up to six people and materials, though most people travel by ramp. A hoist breakdown stops ore delivery, so the hoist is checked before every shift and can run at most about 16 hours a day.

evidence.note: Section 16.4.

process_map.name: Surface ore stockpile and mill feed
process_map.description: Ore from the shaft bin and the open pit is stockpiled by source and grade, then reclaimed with a loader to the crusher following the metallurgist's blend. Mixed or misreported piles distort the reconciliation between mine and mill.

evidence.note: Ore from underground and the open pit fed one mill; a stockpile of over 40,000 t from the pit was milled in 2021.

process_map.name: Stope backfilling
process_map.description: Services crews place waste rock, sometimes with cement, into mined-out stopes after the cavity survey, building fill fences and tipping or pushing the fill with LHDs. Delayed backfill holds up adjacent stopes and adds stability risk.

evidence.note: Backfill with paste or rock is used at comparable Ontario mines; rockfill assumed for a smaller mine.

process_map.name: Underground services installation
process_map.description: A services crew extends compressed air, water, power, ventilation duct, leaky feeder radio and pumping to new headings, and builds refuge stations and electrical substations. Development stalls when services lag behind the face.

evidence.note: Services are extended every few rounds in each active heading.

process_map.name: Explosives receipt, storage and issue
process_map.description: The magazine attendant receives explosives and detonators from the licensed supplier, stores them in separate licensed magazines, issues them to crews against signed slips and reconciles stock daily. Federal licence conditions and inspections make record errors serious.

evidence.note: Weekly deliveries by a licensed supplier and daily magazine records under a Natural Resources Canada magazine licence; common practice.

process_map.name: Open pit mining by contractor
process_map.description: The mining contractor drills, blasts, loads and hauls ore and waste from the satellite pit to the plan, while the owner's supervisor checks ore boundaries, haul counts and safety and certifies quantities for payment. Dilution at ore contacts drives the grade delivered.

evidence.note: Satellite pit milled 46,405 t in 2019 and 39,856 t in 2020 and was mined out in Q4 2020; Ontario open pit practice outsources blasting.

process_map.name: Mine dewatering
process_map.description: Pump stations on several levels move water from sumps up the shaft to surface settling ponds; services workers clean sumps and electricians maintain pumps. Spring melt raises inflow and a pump failure can flood lower levels.

evidence.note: Permit to Take Water allows mine dewatering up to 2,273 L/min all year at the reference mine.
Snowmelt in April and May in the Wawa area; multiplier is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Life-of-mine and annual production plan
process_map.description: Engineering turns the reserve estimate into a year-by-year schedule of development, stopes, tonnes, grade, capital and cost, and the annual production plan behind the budget. Changes in reserves, gold price or ventilation capacity force replanning.

evidence.note: Annual plan with a mid-year revision is common practice for TSX producers.

process_map.name: Monthly and weekly mine plan
process_map.description: Mine engineers schedule next month's headings, stopes, backfill and development metres to meet tonnes and grade, using last month's reconciliation and equipment availability, then split it into weekly targets. Late stope releases and reconciliation surprises cause frequent revisions.

evidence.note: Monthly plan with weekly updates is standard practice at underground mines.

process_map.name: Stope design and release
process_map.description: An engineer designs the stope shape and drill rings from the geology model, the geotechnical engineer reviews spans and support, and the package is signed by geology, engineering and operations before release. Rework when new assays change the ore outline is common.

evidence.note: One package per stope; sign-off by geology, engineering and operations is common practice.

process_map.name: Face mapping, sampling and grade control
process_map.description: After each round in an ore heading a geologist maps the face, takes chip samples, marks ore and waste limits and updates the grade control model when assays return; miners take a muck sample from each truck they load. Waste development is not sampled. Assay turnaround and inconsistent sampling decide how much waste is sent to the mill.

evidence.note: Section 11.1: chip samples on ore faces and muck samples taken by miners during loading. The count of 40 to 100 faces a month (one per 3 to 4 m round in ore) is the workflow author's estimate. Previously 130.

process_map.name: Mine survey and cavity monitoring
process_map.description: Surveyors mark heading lines and grades, pick up as-built development, scan emptied stopes with a cavity monitoring system and measure monthly advance and stockpiles. Survey backlog delays backfill and month-end figures.

evidence.note: Daily line and grade work plus stope scans and month-end measurement.

process_map.name: Mine-to-mill reconciliation
process_map.description: Each month engineering and geology compare planned, mined, hoisted and milled tonnes, grade and ounces using survey, tallies and the metallurgical balance, and explain differences. Large unexplained gaps point to dilution, sampling bias or tallies that do not match.

evidence.note: Monthly reconciliation is common practice and is reported in NI 43-101 technical reports.

process_map.name: Ground control program and geotechnical review
process_map.description: The geotechnical engineer maintains the ground control program, reviews stope designs and support records, inspects headings with supervisors and investigates falls of ground. Seismic events or poor ground at depth add urgent reviews.

evidence.note: Support classes, factors of safety and support before entry are documented at a comparable mine.

process_map.name: Definition drilling program
process_map.description: Mine geologists plan underground holes to firm up stopes a year or two ahead, supervise the drilling contractor, log and sample core and send samples to the lab. Drill rig access and assay turnaround limit how quickly new stopes are released.

evidence.note: 2021 guidance included 50,000 m of underground definition drilling at the mine; holes of 100-250 m.

process_map.name: Annual mineral resource and reserve estimate
process_map.description: Geology rebuilds the block model with the year's drilling, engineering applies stope shapes, costs and gold price, and an independent qualified person reviews before the statement is published. Tight disclosure deadlines and audit questions compress the work into a few weeks.

evidence.note: Annual reserve updates are published; the reserve stood at 1.2 Mt at 14.4 g/t after the 2019 update.

process_map.name: Ventilation planning and air quality
process_map.description: An engineer plans airflow for new headings and diesel equipment, runs ventilation surveys and gas checks with crews, and sets fan and regulator changes. Ventilation capacity limits how many diesel units can work at once.

evidence.note: A ventilation upgrade in Q1 2021 was needed to lift the mining rate above 600 tpd.

process_map.name: Crushing
process_map.description: Surface trucks bring ore 16.6 km from the mine portal pad to the mill stockpile, and crusher operators feed it through the jaw and cone crushers and screens to the fine ore bin, removing tramp steel and clearing chokes. Crusher breakdowns are the most common cause of lost milling time.

evidence.note: Two-stage crushing; six days of milling lost to cone crusher downtime in December 2020 (src1); cone crusher replaced in the August 2021 shutdown (er2022).

process_map.name: Grinding, gravity, leaching and Merrill-Crowe precipitation
process_map.description: Control room operators run the ball mills, the gravity concentrator and shaking table, the cyanide leach tanks, the drum filters that recover the gold-bearing solution and the Merrill-Crowe circuit, where zinc dust precipitates gold that is caught in sock presses. They adjust grind, density, cyanide and pH against shift samples around the clock. Gravity recovers about 43% of the gold and precipitation most of the rest, 97% overall. Feed changes, power dips and pump failures upset recovery.

evidence.note: Section 17 and Table 17-1; 97.7% recovery on underground ore in 2020 (src1).

process_map.name: Refining precipitate and gravity concentrate to doré
process_map.description: Every two weeks the loaded press socks are taken out and burned in the sock oven, and about weekly the shaking table concentrate is collected. Gold room operators mix each concentrate with fluxes, smelt it in the furnace and pour doré bars of 80 to 94% gold under two-person rule and camera coverage. Each bar is weighed, sampled and recorded before going to the vault.
process_map.unit_of_work: one smelt and pour batch (precipitate or table concentrate)

evidence.note: Sections 17.3.5 and 17.3.7; batch count is the workflow author's estimate from the two-weekly sock change and weekly table cleanup.

process_map.name: Doré shipment to refinery
process_map.description: The mill superintendent and security prepare a shipment, seal the bars, hand them to the armed carrier against signed manifests and send the shipment advice to finance and the Royal Canadian Mint. The site controller records the doré in transit. Weather and carrier schedules set the timing.

evidence.note: The 2016 report names the Royal Canadian Mint; two to four shipments a month is the original author's estimate.

process_map.name: Tailings management
process_map.description: Leached slurry is washed and dewatered on drum filters in the tailings building, and the filter cake is conveyed and trucked to the tailings area, where a dozer spreads it along the dam crest. Technicians read pond levels and piezometers, and the engineer of record inspects the dams yearly. Spring melt and heavy rain raise pond levels and inspection frequency.

evidence.note: Sections 17.3.6 and 20.3: filtered tailings deposited by haul trucks since 2007.
Pond level checks and inspections increase during snowmelt and storms.

process_map.name: Water management and batch effluent treatment
process_map.description: Runoff from the tailings area collects in the reclaim pond, which supplies the mill. Operators add hydrogen peroxide to destroy cyanide, send excess water through the treatment plant (hydroxide, flocculant and geotube filtration) to the polishing pond, and in high-flow periods pump it to the mined-out Mishi pit for storage. Treated water leaves the polishing pond at controlled rates through most of the year. Freshet volumes and tighter limits from January 2021 strain the system.

evidence.note: Sections 17.3.8 and 20.3.3.
Snowmelt brings most of the year's runoff in about a month.

process_map.name: Metallurgical accounting
process_map.description: The metallurgist compiles daily tonnes, head grade, tails grade and recovery from shift logs and assays, and at month end trues up gold in circuit and produced ounces against refinery outturns. Errors here change reported production and the reconciliation.

evidence.note: Daily balance with monthly adjustment to refinery outturn is standard mill practice.

process_map.name: Assay office (Wawa)
process_map.description: A company shuttle brings face, muck, process and some definition samples 1.5 hours by road to the assay office in Wawa every day. Technicians dry, crush and pulverise them, fire assay them in furnace batches of 28 positions with gravimetric or AA finish, insert standards and blanks, and email results to geology and the mill. The office is not accredited and also assays a neighbouring mine's production samples. Backlogs delay grade decisions underground.

evidence.note: Section 11 of both reports; batch count is the workflow author's estimate from sample volumes.

process_map.name: Reagent receiving and handling
process_map.description: Operators receive bulk sodium cyanide, zinc dust, lead nitrate, lime, flocculant, diatomaceous earth and hydrogen peroxide, mix and store them under the cyanide handling procedure, and track consumption. Cyanide deliveries need trained staff, emergency kits and a clear unloading area.

evidence.note: Reagent list from section 17; weekly deliveries are the original author's estimate.

process_map.name: Metallurgical testwork and process improvement
process_map.description: Metallurgists test grind, reagent and circuit changes on plant data and send samples for outside testwork when ore types change. Changes go through a trial and a written change before the plant adopts them.

evidence.note: Small mills run a few trials a year.

process_map.name: Maintenance planning and scheduling
process_map.description: Planners turn preventive maintenance due dates, inspection findings and backlog work requests into a weekly schedule, kit parts and book shutdown windows with operations. Missing parts and urgent breakdowns break the schedule most weeks.

evidence.note: Weekly scheduling is standard practice; schedule compliance in mining is often well under target.

process_map.name: Mobile equipment preventive maintenance
process_map.description: Mechanics service jumbos, loaders, trucks and bolters every 250 hours in the underground or surface shop, following checklists, taking oil samples and logging defects. The unit is out of production while serviced, so PM competes with production for machines.

evidence.note: About 40 units at 350-450 hours a month with a 250-hour service interval.

process_map.name: Breakdown repair
process_map.description: Operators radio a breakdown, the supervisor sends a mechanic, electrician or millwright, who diagnoses the fault, waits for parts if needed and returns the unit to service. Underground access, parts on site and trade availability set the downtime.

evidence.note: Breakdowns outnumber planned jobs in mid-size underground fleets.

process_map.name: Fixed plant maintenance
process_map.description: Millwrights and welders maintain crushers, mills, pumps, tanks, fans and compressors to the weekly schedule, replacing liners and wear parts and doing condition checks. Wear parts with long lead times must be ordered well ahead.

evidence.note: Planned jobs across the mill, hoist plant and surface pumps.

process_map.name: Planned mill and hoist shutdowns
process_map.description: Once a year the mill stops for one to three weeks for major work, as in August 2021 when the cone crusher and trash screen were replaced and the secondary ball mill inspected, and several times a year the mill or hoist stops for one to four days to reline mills, replace pumps and complete inspections, with extra contractors on site. Scope creep, late parts and lockout coordination decide whether the plant restarts on time.

evidence.note: Table 17-1 note on the August 2021 shutdown; the count of short stops is the original author's estimate.

process_map.name: Electrical and power distribution maintenance
process_map.description: Electricians maintain the substation, underground power cables, substations, motors and controls, test ground fault protection and restore power after outages from the grid line. Grid outages stop pumping and ventilation and trigger an emergency response.

evidence.note: Planned and reactive electrical work; a remote site fed by one grid transmission line is assumed.

process_map.name: Hoist and shaft inspections
process_map.description: Millwrights and electricians carry out daily, weekly and periodic hoist, rope, brake and shaft inspections required by regulation, record them and fix defects before the hoist returns to service. A failed test stops hoisting.

evidence.note: Ontario Regulation 854 sets hoist inspection and testing duties (regulation page not opened); weekly cadence summarises daily and periodic checks.

process_map.name: Component rebuilds
process_map.description: Mechanics remove failed or end-of-life engines, transmissions and hydraulic parts, send them to OEM or rebuild shops and track the rotable spares back into stores. Long turnaround leaves units parked.

evidence.note: A fleet of about 40 units generates a handful of major rebuilds a month.

process_map.name: Surface infrastructure and road maintenance
process_map.description: Trades and contractors maintain buildings, the camp, the access road, ponds and pipelines, and plow snow so crews and deliveries can reach site. Winter storms and spring road damage take priority over planned work.

evidence.note: Remote northern Ontario site with its own access road.
Northern Ontario winters; plowing and road work dominate during storms.

process_map.name: Workplace inspections and health and safety committee
process_map.description: Supervisors examine each workplace every shift, the joint health and safety committee inspects monthly, and Ministry inspectors visit; hazards go into work requests and corrective actions are tracked to close. Overdue actions are a common audit finding.

evidence.note: Ontario OHSA requires workplace inspections and a joint health and safety committee (not opened); volumes are the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Incident reporting and investigation
process_map.description: Workers report injuries, near misses, equipment damage and spills; the safety coordinator records them, leads investigations for serious events and tracks corrective actions. Critical injuries must be reported to the Ministry immediately and the scene preserved.

evidence.note: Mid-size underground mines log tens of incidents and near misses a month; critical injury notification under the OHSA (not opened).

process_map.name: Mandatory and task training
process_map.description: Trainers deliver Ontario common core modules to new miners, task training and sign-offs on equipment, and refresher courses, and keep records that supervisors check before assigning work. Untrained workers cannot be lined up, so training backlogs limit crews.

evidence.note: Ontario requires modular common core training for new underground miners (program page not opened).

process_map.name: Emergency preparedness and mine rescue
process_map.description: The HSE team maintains the emergency response plan, refuge stations and stench gas warning, runs evacuation drills, and trains volunteer mine rescue teams with Ontario Mine Rescue. Teams must be ready on every rotation.

evidence.note: Ontario law requires every underground mine to have a mine rescue program and emergency response plan; training through closed courses at sites.

process_map.name: Environmental monitoring and effluent reporting
process_map.description: Technicians sample the mill polishing pond discharge and the mine settling pond discharge to Lake C7 weekly and send monthly toxicity samples to an accredited lab; the coordinator checks results against federal and provincial limits and files quarterly and annual reports. Mill effluent leaves at controlled rates through most of the year. A failed toxicity test raises sampling frequency and must be reported at once.
process_map.unit_of_work: one weekly effluent sampling event at one final discharge point

evidence.note: MDMER weekly sampling and monthly toxicity tests (src7); two continuous discharge points (er2022, section 20.4).
Batch discharges and surface water sampling concentrate in the ice-free months.

process_map.name: Permits, approvals and closure plan
process_map.description: The environmental coordinator tracks approvals and their conditions, prepares applications and amendments for new projects, files closure plan amendments with financial assurance, and answers ministry questions. Permit lead times often set project schedules.

evidence.note: Comparable Ontario mines hold closure plans with ENDM, ECAs and several Permits to Take Water; the reference mine renews a PTTW with MECP.

process_map.name: Indigenous and community relations
process_map.description: The coordinator implements agreements with nearby First Nations, sharing hiring and contracting opportunities, reporting on commitments, and consulting on permits and plans. Missed notifications or commitments damage trust and can delay approvals.

evidence.note: Ontario mines typically operate under impact benefit or similar agreements with nearby First Nations; agreement terms are confidential.

process_map.name: Occupational hygiene monitoring
process_map.description: Safety staff measure diesel particulate, noise, silica dust and gases underground and in the mill, compare them with exposure limits and recommend ventilation or equipment changes. Results feed the ventilation plan and workplace inspections.

evidence.note: Periodic sampling campaigns are common practice in Ontario underground mines.

process_map.name: Purchasing
process_map.description: Buyers turn approved requisitions into purchase orders, get quotes for larger items, expedite urgent parts to site, and keep contracts with key suppliers. Remote location and long lead times make expediting a large share of the work.

evidence.note: Typical PO volume for a remote mine; approval limits by role.
Shutdown scopes add a burst of orders and expediting.

process_map.name: Receiving, stores and inventory
process_map.description: Warehouse attendants receive deliveries against purchase orders, issue parts to mechanics and crews, store rotable components, and count inventory. Unrecorded issues and parts taken underground without a slip spoil inventory accuracy.

evidence.note: Several thousand stores transactions a month for a remote mine.

process_map.name: Accounts payable
process_map.description: Site accountants match supplier invoices to purchase orders and receipts, route invoices without a match for approval, code contractor invoices to approved certificates and prepare weekly payment runs. Price and quantity mismatches and missing receipts cause rework.

evidence.note: About three invoices per PO plus contractor and freight invoices.

process_map.name: Timekeeping and payroll
process_map.description: Supervisors submit crew timesheets with overtime, shift premiums and bonus metres; payroll administrators check them, enter them into the payroll service and process biweekly pay. Bonus calculations and rotation schedules cause most corrections.

evidence.note: Biweekly payroll for about 300 employees with production bonuses.

process_map.name: Recruitment and onboarding
process_map.description: HR coordinators post positions, screen and interview candidates with supervisors, run pre-employment medicals and references, and onboard new hires into training and rotation. Skilled trades and experienced miners are hard to find in the north.

evidence.note: Turnover of 15-25% a year in a 300-person mining workforce.

process_map.name: Crew rotation travel and camp booking
process_map.description: Site administrators book buses, flights and camp rooms for each crew change and for contractors, issue the crew manifest to the gate and handle last-minute swaps. Weather and road closures disrupt crew changes.

evidence.note: Mill crews rotate seven days in and seven out (er2016) and underground crews on longer rotations (assumed 14/14), so a crew changes about every week.

process_map.name: Camp and catering services
process_map.description: A catering contractor runs the camp kitchen, housekeeping and rooms; site administration allocates rooms, handles complaints and allocates occupancy costs to departments. Contractor surges can overflow the camp.

evidence.note: Comparable mines provide temporary accommodation for non-local staff; contracted catering is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Monthly site cost reporting and forecast
process_map.description: The site controller closes the month, accrues unbilled work, explains cost variances with department heads, calculates cost per tonne and per ounce, and updates the full-year forecast for head office. Late receipts and contractor accruals drive most adjustments.

evidence.note: Monthly close in the ERP with workbook variance analysis is common practice.

process_map.name: IT and communications support
process_map.description: IT technicians set up accounts, computers and radios for new staff, fix network, leaky feeder and ERP access problems, and work with head office on backups and security. A single remote network link makes outages hard to fix.

evidence.note: Help desk volume for about 350 people on site.

process_map.name: Site access and gold security
process_map.description: Security officers control the gate against crew manifests, search vehicles and people leaving the mill area, monitor the gold room cameras, and log every entry to secure areas. Gold theft risk makes these logs a key control.

evidence.note: Around-the-clock security is common at gold mills.

process_map.name: Contractor management
process_map.description: Site management prequalifies contractors, checks insurance and safety documents, orients crews on arrival, supervises their work and approves quantities for payment. Poor contractor safety performance is a frequent incident source.

evidence.note: Shutdown, drilling, construction and catering contractors rotate through site.

process_map.name: Fuel and lubricant supply
process_map.description: Fuel is delivered to surface tanks, transferred to underground fuel bays, and dispensed by unit with meter readings logged for cost allocation and equipment hours. Gaps in fuel records hide leaks and theft.

evidence.note: Weekly bulk diesel deliveries for a diesel underground fleet.

process_map.name: Exploration program planning
process_map.description: The VP and exploration manager rank targets near the mine and on the Quebec and regional properties, set metres and budgets, and present the program with the annual budget. Results during the year shift money between targets.

evidence.note: 2021 program of C$16M at the mine and C$16M in Quebec with drilling metres by type.

process_map.name: Surface exploration drilling
process_map.description: Project geologists site holes, arrange access and permits, supervise contract rigs that drill around the clock, check daily drill reports and close holes with downhole surveys. Winter freeze-up gives access to swampy ground and drives a drilling peak.

evidence.note: 2021 surface exploration guidance of 54,000 m at the mine and 42,000 m in Quebec, at roughly 300-500 m per hole.

surge.cause: winter drilling season on frozen ground

evidence.note: Swampy targets are drilled after freeze-up in January to March.

process_map.name: Core logging and sampling
process_map.description: Geologists log lithology, alteration and veining and mark sample intervals; core technicians photograph, saw and bag samples with standards and blanks and ship them to a commercial lab. Core backlogs build when several rigs run at once.

evidence.note: Drill core at comparable mines goes to commercial labs while production samples stay local.

process_map.name: Drill data QA/QC and database
process_map.description: The database geologist loads logs, surveys and assay certificates, checks standards, blanks and duplicates, flags failures for re-assay and releases validated intercepts. Results cannot be disclosed until QA/QC passes.

evidence.note: Commercial labs return certificates of 20-50 samples.

process_map.name: Claims, permits and assessment filings
process_map.description: The database geologist tracks claim anniversaries in the Ontario and Quebec online systems, applies for exploration permits and files assessment work reports so claims stay in good standing. A missed date can forfeit ground.

evidence.note: Ontario moved to online cell claims in 2018 and Quebec uses map-designated cells; filings are spread through the year.

process_map.name: Exploration project evaluation
process_map.description: Geologists model promising zones, estimate a first resource with consultants, and prepare a study proposal if the target could feed the mill or restart the Quebec property. Most targets do not reach this stage.

evidence.note: Reference company published an updated Kiena Deep resource and planned a PEA in 2020.

process_map.name: Care and maintenance of the Quebec property
process_map.description: A small team keeps the idle Quebec shaft, mill and tailings in safe condition, pumps water, completes required inspections and reports, and hosts the drilling program. Costs are reported to head office each month.
process_map.unit_of_work: one month of care and maintenance

evidence.note: Kiena on care and maintenance since 2013 with a 930 m shaft and 2,000 tpd permitted mill.

process_map.name: Gold sales and settlement
process_map.description: When the refinery credits ounces to the metal account, the treasury manager sells them at spot to a financial institution, checks the refinery outturn against the shipment, and the corporate controller matches the trade before it is recorded. The company had no gold forward contracts in 2020 or 2021. Timing and price decisions are approved by the CFO.

evidence.note: 91,229 oz sold in 2020 for C$215.3M (src1); spot sales to financial institutions only (wdofs2021).

process_map.name: Quarterly financial reporting
process_map.description: Corporate finance consolidates site and head-office results, prepares IFRS statements and the MD&A with non-IFRS cost measures, supports the auditor's review, and files after audit committee approval. Deadlines are 45 days after each quarter and 90 days after year end.

evidence.note: National Instrument 51-102 filing deadlines for non-venture issuers (not opened); common practice.
Annual audit and statements carry more work than a quarterly review.

process_map.name: Annual information form and technical disclosure
process_map.description: Legal and finance prepare the annual information form with reserves, risks and operations; qualified persons sign technical content and an NI 43-101 technical report is filed when results change materially. Consistency across documents is checked line by line.

evidence.note: Technical reports filed under NI 43-101 by comparable producers.

process_map.name: Treasury and cash management
process_map.description: The treasury manager forecasts cash, funds site payment runs, manages the credit facility and covenants and invests surplus cash, reporting to the CFO and audit committee. Gold price swings move the forecast quickly.

evidence.note: Weekly cash management for a single-asset producer.

process_map.name: Investor relations and news releases
process_map.description: Investor relations drafts production, results and exploration news releases with qualified person review, hosts calls and site visits, and answers shareholder and analyst questions. Selective disclosure rules shape every contact.

evidence.note: Quarterly production and results releases plus exploration updates are common practice.

process_map.name: Board and committee governance
process_map.description: The corporate secretary prepares board and committee packages, minutes and resolutions for quarterly statements, budgets, health and safety, and major projects, and organises the annual meeting. Late papers shorten review time.

evidence.note: Quarterly board meetings with audit, compensation, HSE and technical committees.

process_map.name: Annual budget and guidance
process_map.description: Head office combines the site plan, exploration program and corporate costs into a budget and public guidance, tests it against gold price and cost scenarios, and takes it to the board in December. Site and head office often iterate several times.

evidence.note: Production, cost, capital and exploration guidance published each January.

process_map.name: Mining tax and royalties
process_map.description: The treasury and tax manager calculates net smelter return royalties from sales each quarter, pays royalty holders, and prepares Ontario mining tax and income tax instalments and returns with outside advisers. Royalty boundaries and deductions need careful records.

evidence.note: Several NSR royalties apply to parts of the comparable Wawa-area mine; Ontario mining tax rules not opened.

process_map.name: Insurance and enterprise risk
process_map.description: Legal and finance renew property, business interruption, liability and directors' insurance with a broker each year, and maintain the risk register reviewed by the board. Underwriter site surveys add work in renewal months.

evidence.note: Annual renewal and quarterly risk review are common practice.

process_map.name: Capital project approval and delivery
process_map.description: The COO's team reviews proposals such as a ventilation upgrade, tailings raise or equipment replacement, seeks board approval above limits, secures permits and tracks spending and schedule. Permitting and contractor availability decide timing.

evidence.note: 2021 growth capital of C$22-26M including a ventilation upgrade, electric equipment and zone development.

process_map.name: Compensation, benefits and HR policy
process_map.description: The HR director sets pay scales, bonus plans and benefits, benchmarks against northern Ontario mines, and updates HR policies used by the site. Tight labour markets for miners and trades push wage reviews.

evidence.note: Annual compensation review is common practice.

process_map.name: Corporate development
process_map.description: Executives screen acquisition, joint venture and royalty opportunities, visit properties, run due diligence on geology, permits and costs with consultants, and bring the few promising proposals to the board. Most screened opportunities are dropped after a desktop review.

evidence.note: Junior and mid-tier producers screen opportunities continually.

assumptions: The file describes a composite single-mine producer for 2019-2022. It follows Wesdome before its Kiena restart: the Quebec property is treated as an exploration and care-and-maintenance project, not a second mine. Wesdome restarted Kiena in 2021-2022, which this file leaves out.

Underground headcounts follow Table 16-10 of the 2022 technical report; other headcounts are the original author's estimates from crew sizes for a 600-1,100 tpd underground mine with 12-hour shifts. Mill crews rotate seven days in and seven out (er2016); the underground rotation is assumed to be 14 on and 14 off. A role's headcount includes contractor staff who do the same work, recorded in contractor_headcount and left out of the employee count. Contractors for drilling, catering, shutdowns and the open pit are external parties.

Loaded cost per hour is base wage or salary times 1.30 for office and staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles (benefits, payroll taxes, rotation and northern allowances and production bonus); camp and travel costs are excluded. Executive rates use cash compensation only. 2024-2025 Job Bank wages were deflated by about 10% to the 2019-2022 period.

Operating cost per tonne at comparable Ontario underground mines ranges from about C$170 to C$310 per tonne milled (src4, src5); site process volumes were sized to be consistent with that scale of spending.

Regulatory duties under Ontario Regulation 854, the OHSA, the Mining Act and NI 51-102 are described from general knowledge because the e-Laws and OSC pages could not be opened; those processes carry tier C evidence.
The mill averaged 779 t/d in 2021-2022, with a maximum day of 1,027 t/d (er2022, Table 17-1).
Process volumes in cases_per_month for annual or quarterly processes are fractions (one annual cycle is about 0.08 a month).
Occupation codes use NOC 2016, the version in force for most of 2019-2022.
